equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet; non-marketable private equity stakes, includes 367 of unrealised gains booked in 9M-2026. Illiquid; carrying value is not a market price.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward run-rate: Q3-2026 cRPO +20% and revenue +20.5% including roughly 4 points from Armis, Moveworks and Veza; organic about 16-17%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (35.5% over five years) is more than 30% above the revenue CAGR (24.1%) and is not a usable growth anchor: book equity is inflated by SBC credited to paid-in capital and by the FY2023 valuation-allowance release. EPS CAGRs are distorted by the same release and a near-zero FY2020 base.
historical_growth.notes: Fiscal years FY2020, FY2022, FY2025. Owner FCF = OCF less capex less SBC less interest income: FY2025 4,576 - 1,955 - 451 = 2,170; FY2022 2,173 - 1,401 - 82 = 690; FY2020 1,367 - 870 - ~40 = ~457 (FY2020 interest income is not in the extracted filings and is an estimate). Owner FCF grew FASTER than reported FCF because SBC fell from 19% of revenue in FY2020-22 to 14.7% in FY2025. That has reversed in 2026: SBC is 15.4% of Q3-2026 revenue and nine-month RSU grants were 33.1m shares at a 105.76 average (about 3.5bn of grant value, 0.6bn of it Armis) against a 2.3bn TTM expense. EPS is split-adjusted: FY2022 1.60 and FY2020 0.59 pre-split are 0.32 and 0.118 post-split against FY2025 1.67.

scenario_narratives.base: ServiceNow stays the system of action for large-enterprise IT, employee and customer workflows: the renewal rate holds at 98%, customers above USD 5m of ACV keep compounding (680, up 23%), and AI agent products and the security acquisitions (Armis, Veza) replace the slowing core as the growth leg. Organic growth nonetheless keeps decelerating from about 16-17% toward mid-single digits over the decade as the installed base saturates. Margins rise slowly, about half a point a year, because AI inference and hyperscaler hosting keep subscription gross margin structurally below the 80%+ of 2022-25 (74% in Q3-2026, of which roughly five points is acquired-intangible amortisation). SBC drifts down from 15% to 11% of revenue, still heavy for a mature software company.
scenario_narratives.bull: Agentic AI is additive rather than cannibalising: consumption-priced AI agents and the AI control-tower positioning lift net expansion, security becomes a second multi-billion franchise on the Armis and Veza base, and growth holds near 20% for two more years before fading. Scale and a lower share-price-driven grant burden take SBC to 9% of revenue and EBITDA margin to 43%, with stronger billings keeping deferred-revenue inflows at 20% of revenue growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI agents reduce the number of human seats that fulfilment, service-desk and HR workflows need, and customers and hyperscaler-native agents push back on per-seat pricing: growth drops to low double digits next year and to GDP-like rates by year seven. The 9bn of 2026 acquisitions turn out to have bought growth that was slowing organically; integration and severance costs recur, AI compute keeps gross margin under pressure, and EBITDA margin stalls at 34-35%. With the share price lower, retention grants keep SBC at 13-15% of revenue. Exit multiple capped at 15x for an ex-growth software vendor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF basis: stock compensation is charged in full as a cash-equivalent cost and the share count is held flat, so buybacks are value-neutral. On that basis ServiceNow's TTM owner FCF is about 2.1bn against 4.75bn reported; the gap between the house and street values is almost entirely the treatment of roughly 2.3bn a year of SBC. Value is terminal-heavy and depends on SBC falling as a share of revenue while margins expand.
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC ratio: each point of terminal SBC-to-revenue is worth several dollars a share; 2026 grant value (about 3.5bn in nine months) is running well ahead of the expense, so the 0.5 point a year decline is not yet visible in the filings
Net-share-settlement taxes (TTM 598, FY2025 770) are a real cash cost of holding the count flat that is not charged on top of the SBC expense; charging them as well would lower every scenario
Organic growth is not disclosed; the split between organic and acquired growth is an estimate from purchase-price disclosures
Balance sheet has moved from 8.6bn net cash at Dec 2025 to 0.6bn net debt; 2.1bn of commercial paper needs rolling or repaying from cash
Strategic investments (2.05bn) are illiquid private stakes carried above cost
Seat-based pricing exposure to AI agents; subscription gross margin down from 80% to 74% in a year
Cash tax rate (about 12% of owner EBIT today) is assumed to normalise to 21% by year six; Pillar 2 or faster exhaustion of deductions would pull that forward

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 81.24-175.00
data_sources.financials: SEC filings: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026 (balance sheet, cash flow, EPS note, equity awards, debt, non-GAAP reconciliations) and Form 10-K FY2025; history from NOW.duckdb core_metrics and kpis
data_sources.qualitative: 10-K FY2025 and Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A, business-combination and debt notes. NOW_Analysis.json was not available at build time.

inputs.share_count_basis: Post-split (5-for-1 effective 2025-12-17). 1,037.9m shares outstanding on the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet plus 8.1m treasury-method dilution (Q3-2026 diluted weighted average 1,043.0m less basic 1,034.9m; 10-Q EPS note). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Unvested awards (41.8m RSUs, 6.9m options) are not added on top: their cost is the forward SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Company's non-GAAP income-from-operations reconciliation line 'Stock-based compensation': FY2025 1,955 (10-K) less 9M-2025 1,461 plus 9M-2026 1,846 (Q3-2026 10-Q) = TTM 2,340. Cash-flow add-back is 1,955 / 1,461 / 1,829 (TTM 2,323). Taxes paid on net share settlement (TTM 598; FY2025 770) are NOT summed on top, per the house rule against adding the add-back and the withholding line; they are recorded as a memo. ServiceNow publishes no single combined figure.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.4% (10-year UST; consistent with the company's May-2036 notes priced at 5.40% in May 2026), equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.05 gives cost of equity ~9.7%. Debt is ~7% of enterprise value at ~4% after tax, so WACC rounds to 9.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities (891) are NOT in net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, SaaS). Fresh build, no prior valuation. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026 rather than FY2025, so that the flow base and the balance sheet share one date: the September balance sheet already contains nine months of 2026 cash flow, USD 9.2bn of cash paid for Armis (Apr 2026, 7.6bn), Veza (Mar 2026, 1.2bn) and others, USD 2.2bn of buybacks, and the USD 4.0bn notes plus 2.1bn commercial paper raised to fund them. Year 1 is therefore the twelve months to Sep 2027. TTM figures are FY2025 less 9M-2025 plus 9M-2026, all actuals. Net debt = commercial paper 2,086 + senior notes 5,438 (carrying value) less cash 2,393, marketable securities 2,214 and long-term marketable securities 2,354. Strategic investments (2,050, private equity stakes at cost adjusted for observable prices) are added in the equity bridge at carrying value because none of their gains are in the flows. Interest income (TTM 332) is stripped from last_fcf: the company held net cash of ~8.6bn for most of the period; it is now marginally net debt, and the forward build is unlevered so neither interest income nor interest expense enters it. EBITDA margin is company non-GAAP operating income (before SBC, purchased-intangible amortisation, deal costs, severance) plus depreciation: TTM 4,811 + 732 = 5,543, 35.9% of revenue. D&A path is depreciation only (acquired-intangible amortisation, TTM 535, is treated as non-deductible, which is conservative for cash tax). Buybacks: TTM 2,822 of actual financing outflow, including a 2.0bn ASR in Q1-2026; none in Q3-2026; 4.2bn of authorisation remains. The flat share count is funded: the company is an active repurchaser. Share basis: all per-share figures are post-split. Core_metrics quarterly share counts and EPS for 2024 and earlier are pre-split (about 206m shares) while FY2023-FY2025 annual rows are restated; the historical EPS CAGRs below divide pre-split EPS by five. Qualitative Analysis JSON was not present at build time; scenario axes are drawn from the 10-K and 10-Q.

base.rationale: Year-1 growth 17% = ~15.5-16% organic plus ~1.5 points from a full year of Armis. Year-1 EBITDA margin 35.5% is below the TTM 35.9% because half of the 1.2% of revenue the company excludes as severance is treated as recurring. SBC starts at the TTM 15.2% and declines ~0.5 points a year. Cash tax starts near the TTM 12% of owner EBIT (300 paid on 2,471) and ramps to 21%. Working-capital capture 15% of the revenue increase, matching the TTM (~400 on a 2,764 increase after adding back deal and severance cash). Capex 3.3-3.5% of revenue reflects the 2026 step-down (9M 346 against 630) as hosting moves to hyperscalers and the cost shows up in gross margin instead.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the thesis now leans on an unproven shift from seat-based to agent/consumption pricing, organic growth is decelerating while 9bn of debt-funded acquisitions mask it, and subscription gross margin has fallen six points in a year. Base 50%: 98% renewals, 29.7bn of RPO and 20% cRPO growth make the middle path well evidenced. Bull cut to 25%: it needs sustained ~20% growth, margin expansion and a falling SBC ratio at the same time, three things 2026 has not shown together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
